messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick discovery follow-up - production readiness questions

Thanks for the call today - that was helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Our traffic pattern is bursty (end of month reports) with spikes up to ~200 concurrent requests.
- Most prompts are short (1-3 sentences) but we have a subset of long-context tickets (~2-3 paragraphs).
- We do have some user-entered PII (emails, order numbers) that we redact before storage.

Samira and I talked about a sample prompt set; we can pull together ~25 prompts that represent the common flows and a few edge cases. I attached an initial CSV export (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with 8 examples - some rows are descriptions rather than verbatim prompts.

Next steps on our side: we'll expand the export to ~25 rows and flag which are sensitive. Can you confirm what you need for the model/eval side (recommended models, benchmarks, redaction guidance)?

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product - Acme Corp

--Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv (text/csv, 8 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit follow-up & prompt set request - Acme

Hi Alex, Samira - thanks for the export and the notes - very helpful context. Recap and request from our side after internal sync:

Recap from call:
- Bursty traffic w/ month-end spikes (~200 concurrent) - that maps well to Redwood Dedicated or a hosted plan with burst policy.
- Prompt length mix: most short, a small long-context cohort - we'll want to validate both latency and quality on longer inputs.
- PII redaction is fine; please mark rows that contain sensitive user data.

What we'll provide (by EOD Friday):
- Recommended model shortlist (open and optimized variants) with estimated cost/latency profiles.
- A lightweight benchmark report (latency and 95th pct costs) for your representative prompt mix: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-model-fit-2026
- A prompt/eval template and labeling guide to help you collect ground-truth outputs for quality regression checks.

What we need from you:
1) Expanded prompt set (20-30 prompts) including 4-6 edge cases (ambiguous phrasing, long context, mixed languages, html fragments). Prefer CSV with columns: id, prompt, category, expected_output_example, sensitive_flag.
2) Any regulatory redaction rules you require (e.g., persist order numbers but strip emails) - if you don't have a policy, we can propose a conservative default.
3) If you have an internal test user account or sample logs we can run against (scrubbed), that helps reproduce real token distributions.

Attachments: please re-attach the security questionnaire if you have it - our security team will start the review.

I'm looping Aditya (solutions) and Neha (security) who'll help with benchmarking and redaction guidance. Proposed timeline: we'll send the model shortlist + initial benchmarks by Fri (2026-03-06). If you can get the full prompt set by Tue (2026-03-09), we'll run the eval and share results by Thu (2026-03-12).

Thanks - looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142

Quick internal + to-customer note:

Marissa - we'll prepare the shortlist with two tiers: (A) lowest-latency variants optimized for short prompts and (B) higher-context variants tuned for long-ticket quality. I'll include benchmarks for 95th pct latency and cost/token for both. Neha - please draft the redaction recommendations: default to strip emails, hash order ids, and keep timestamps.

Alex/Samira - for CSV format we prefer UTF-8, commas, and the header row exactly as Marissa suggested (id,prompt,category,expected_output_example,sensitive_flag). If you need a template I'll drop a sample CSV into this thread.

Thanks - we'll keep to the timeline.
